dispute.openBody: Three Isoko members who have never worked with either of you will read both sides and decide.
dispute.reason_poorQuality: The work is not what was agreed

dispute.title: Disputes
dispute.subtitle: Disagreements about a job, decided by three independent workers.
dispute.noResponse: The other party has not responded yet.
dispute.addSidePlaceholder: Explain what was agreed and what happened from your side.
dispute.deadline: To be decided by {{date}}, or an admin steps in
dispute.rationalePlaceholder: Why? Shared with the parties once it is decided.
dispute.againstMajority: did not side with the outcome
dispute.panelNote: Drawn at random from {{count}} eligible members.
dispute.withAdmin: The panel could not agree in time; an admin is deciding.
dispute.means_release: The job counts as done. The client pays the full {{amount}} RWF with Mobile Money.
dispute.means_split: The job counts as done. The client pays half the agreed price with Mobile Money.
dispute.means_refund: The job is called off. Nothing is owed.
dispute.how1Body: While a job is under way, waiting to be paid, or up to 14 days after it is paid, the worker or the client explains what went wrong. The other person can add their side.
dispute.how2Body: Three experienced Isoko workers who have never worked with either person read both sides and vote within 5 days.
dispute.how3Body: Full price, half, or nothing. Before payment it sets what the client pays; after payment, what the worker returns.
dispute.reason_notPaid: The client marked the job done but has not paid
dispute.stageBody_in_progress: The job is under way. The decision says whether it counts as done and what the client pays.
dispute.stageBody_awaiting_payment: The job is marked done but not paid. Payment waits until the dispute is decided, and the decision sets what the client owes.
dispute.stageBody_paid: The client has already paid {{amount}} RWF. If the decision goes against the worker, they return all or half of it, and the Isoko team arranges it with you both.
dispute.means_awaiting_payment_release: The client pays the full price with Mobile Money.
dispute.means_awaiting_payment_split: The client pays half the agreed price with Mobile Money.
dispute.means_awaiting_payment_refund: The job is called off. Nothing is owed.
dispute.means_paid_split: The worker returns half, {{half}} RWF, to the client. The Isoko team arranges it.
dispute.means_paid_refund: The worker returns the full {{amount}} RWF to the client. The Isoko team arranges it.
dispute.refundRequest: Follow the refund in Help & support
dispute.opened: Dispute opened. The other person and the panel have been told.
dispute.pickIntro: You can dispute a job while it is under way, while it waits to be paid, and for 14 days after it is paid. Each job can be disputed once.
dispute.pickNone: None of your jobs can be disputed right now.

team.youWereInvited: You were invited to this job as {{role}}.

adminNav.gigApprovalsSub: New gigs wait here until an admin checks them. Approve to put them live; the ranked shortlist is invited at once.
adminNav.skillReviewsSub: Skill submissions waiting on a decision, laid open with their evidence.
adminNav.jobsSub: Work under way and work finished, with where the money stands.
adminNav.paymentsSub: Mobile Money payments: paid, waiting for the client's approval, jobs not yet paid, and transfers to workers.
adminNav.usersSub: Suspend an account to block sign-in immediately, or delete it permanently.
adminNav.reviewersSub: Who reviews skill evidence. Peers are well-rated workers; the rotation rules decide who sees what.
adminNav.auditSub: Signs of reviewers and workers favouring each other. A flag is a prompt to look, not a finding.
adminNav.metricsSub: The measurements behind the research questions: does ranking get work accepted, and do newcomers get a fair start?
adminNav.marketSub: What jobs actually pay in each trade, and why applications are turned down.

fairwork.title: Fairwork scorecard
fairwork.subtitle: Isoko scored against the five Fairwork principles for platform work, from its own records, recomputed every time this page loads.
fairwork.about: Fairwork, at the Oxford Internet Institute, rates gig platforms in 38 countries on fair pay, conditions, contracts, management and representation, two points each. We apply the same principles to ourselves, live, and show the number behind every point.
fairwork.c_payAtFloor: Jobs pay at least the usual low end for the trade
fairwork.c_payAtFloor_d: Share of payouts at or above the 25th percentile of what that trade pays on Isoko.
fairwork.c_noCommission: Workers keep the full agreed price
fairwork.c_noCommission_d: Share of payouts with no platform commission taken from the worker.
fairwork.c_disputesOnTime_d: Share of disputes decided, or still within, the 5 days promised.
fairwork.c_receipts: Every payout has a checkable receipt
fairwork.c_receipts_d: Share of paid jobs that produced receipted payouts.
fairwork.c_explained_d: Share of applications and invitations that carry the reasons behind their ranking.
fairwork.c_appealsHandled_d: Share of appeals against reviewers decided, or still within 14 days.
fairwork.c_reasonsGiven_d: Share of rejected applications that carry a reason.
fairwork.c_peerReviewers_d: Workers enrolled as peer reviewers of skill evidence.
fairwork.c_workerVoice_d: Not in place: workers have no way yet to vote on platform rules.
fairwork.c_paidThroughIsoko_d: Share of finished jobs whose worker was paid through Isoko with Mobile Money.

support.title: Help & support
support.subtitle: Answers to common questions, and a direct line to the Isoko team.
support.heroBody: Search for an answer, or choose a topic. If you still need help, the Isoko team replies here, usually within a day.
support.searchPlaceholder: Search for an answer, e.g. MoMo prompt
support.searchNoResults: No answer matches that. Contact us and we will help.
support.contactCta: Write to us and the Isoko team will reply here, usually within a day.
support.safetyNow: If you are in danger right now, call 112 first. Then tell us here and we will act on it straight away.
support.noRequests: You have not contacted support yet. When you do, your requests and our replies appear here.
support.formIntro: Tell us what happened. The more detail, the faster we can help.
support.subject: Subject
support.subjectPlaceholder: A few words, e.g. Payment not received
support.messagePlaceholder: What happened, and what did you expect? Include dates and amounts if it is about money.
support.messageTooShort: Tell us a little more: at least a sentence.
support.related: Is it about one of these?
support.relatedNone: Not about a specific job or payment
support.attachTooBig: That file is larger than 5 MB.
support.sent: Request {{number}} sent. We will reply here.
support.closeConfirm: Close this request? You can start a new one at any time.

support.ratedNo: We have reopened your request and will look again.
support.waitingHint: The team replied. Answer below so we can carry on.

payment.q1: The Mobile Money prompt did not appear on my phone
payment.a1: Dial *182*7*1# to see payments waiting for your approval and approve it there with your PIN. If it is not listed, open the job and press Pay again; you will not be charged twice.
payment.q2: I paid but the job still says it is waiting
payment.a2: MTN sometimes takes a few minutes to confirm. Isoko checks every minute and the job shows Paid as soon as MTN confirms. If it still waits after an hour, contact us with the time you approved it.
payment.q3: Where do I find my receipt?
payment.a3: Open Wallet. Every paid job has a receipt number; press it to open the receipt, which anyone can check on its public page.

account.a1: On the sign-in page choose “Forgot password?” and enter the email on your account. The link we send works for one hour.
account.q2: My phone code does not arrive
account.a2: Check the number starts with 072, 073, 078 or 079. Codes can take a minute; you can ask for a new one after the countdown. If the number is confirmed on another account, it cannot be used twice.
account.q3: How do I change my profile picture?
account.a3: Go to Settings › Profile, press Upload picture, place your face in the circle and press Done.

skills.q1: How long does a skill review take?
skills.a1: Two experienced workers in your trade review each submission, usually within two days. You get a notification with their decision.
skills.q2: My skill was turned down. What can I do?
skills.a2: The notification says why. You can appeal from Settings › Proof of skill, or send new evidence such as photos of finished work.
skills.a3: Clear photos or a short video of work you did yourself, a certificate, or a reference from someone you worked for.

job.q1: The other person and I disagree about a job
job.a1: From the job card choose “Open a dispute”. Three independent mediators look at what both of you say and decide what is fair.
job.q2: The client has not marked my job as done
job.a2: Send them a message first. If they do not answer, open a dispute: the mediators can mark the job done so you are paid.
job.q3: Someone asked me to pay or be paid outside Isoko
job.a3: Do not. Only payments through Isoko have a receipt, Job Cover and dispute protection. You can report the person from their profile.

safety.q1: I feel unsafe on a job right now
safety.a1: Leave if you can and call 112. On an on-site job, the SOS button alerts your trusted contact and the Isoko team.
safety.q2: How does the safe visit work?
safety.a2: Check in when you arrive and check out when you leave. If you do not check out, your trusted contact and the team are told.
safety.a3: Report them from their profile, or contact us here. Who reported is never shown to the person reported.

bug.q1: A page does not load or shows an error
bug.a1: Check your connection, then reload the page. If it still fails, contact us with a screenshot and what you pressed.
bug.a2: Your actions are saved and sent when the connection returns. You do not need to press again.
bug.q3: The app looks wrong on my phone
bug.a3: Send us a screenshot and the phone model. Turning the phone sideways or updating the browser often helps.

other.a1: During the pilot Isoko charges no fee on jobs. Optional Job Cover is billed with the payment.
other.a2: Yes, please. Contact us with the idea; the team reads every suggestion.
other.q3: How do I delete my account or get my data?
other.a3: Download your data from Settings › Your data. To delete your account, contact us and we will do it.
